articles.title: A day of teamwork, talent and possibility
articles.summary: Highlights from the Ali Garh Model School Sports Gala 2025.
body: PEN shared photographic highlights from the Ali Garh Model School Sports Gala 2025. Explore the event through the original photo feature.
articles.source: Ali Garh Model School Sports Gala 2025

articles.title: Healthier children. Stronger communities.
articles.summary: PEN and IPAC Foundation brought health screening to the Assu Mehta school community.
body: The second annual health screening camp took place at Government Girls Primary School, Assu Mehta, in collaboration with IPAC Foundation.
The initiative reached 83 students, staff members and parents. Services included 73 general checkups, 72 dental screenings and 73 eye screenings, supporting early detection and access to care.

articles.title: Young minds rise to the maths challenge
articles.summary: More than 700 PEN and PEIMA students took part in Pakistan Maths Challenge 2024.
body: Students from Grades 1–10 tested their problem-solving skills in the Pakistan Maths Challenge, hosted by 3P Learning.
PEN reported 57 gold medals and 173 silver medals. The competition celebrated mathematical confidence and the effort of students and teachers.

articles.title: A young writer finds her voice
articles.summary: Komal Latif’s prize-winning essay shows what opportunity can unlock.
body: Komal Latif, a Class VIII student at Government Girls Middle School, Kot Lakhpat, won first prize in an English creative-writing competition with more than 2,000 participants.

Her essay celebrated a hardworking farmer in her neighbourhood. PEN’s academic team helped her return to school after financial pressures interrupted her education. She continued studying while supporting her family, with the ambition of becoming a teacher.

articles.title: An education that changed Sajid’s path
articles.summary: From leaving school to returning with determination and support.
body: When financial hardship interrupted Sajid Ali’s education, PEN’s academic team worked with his family to bring him back to Government Boys Middle School, Sadhoki.

With sponsorship and encouragement, Sajid returned to the classroom. He won a PEN Urdu essay competition and achieved 91% in his Class VIII exams. PEN’s account records that he later joined Punjab Police as a constable.

articles.title: Social media as a learning tool
articles.summary: Exploring digital platforms as a place to learn, connect and collaborate.
body: PEN explores how online platforms can make educational resources easier to access and help learners exchange knowledge.

Used with purpose, video lessons, professional networks and group discussions can complement classroom teaching. The article considers accessibility, collaboration and the changing relationship between technology and education.

articles.title: How education can transform lives
articles.summary: Why learning is the foundation for independence and opportunity.
body: Literacy and numeracy help people make informed decisions in daily life. PEN’s article connects these skills with self-reliance, personal development and wider opportunity.
Education also supports critical thinking and participation in communities. Access to good teaching gives children a stronger foundation for the choices ahead.

articles.title: Education and the cycle of poverty
articles.summary: The connection between access to learning and a more secure future.
body: PEN examines how education can expand employment opportunities and help families improve their circumstances.
The article highlights the importance of access to quality schooling for children from underserved communities, connecting classroom learning with long-term opportunity.

articles.title: Why support Progressive Education Network?
articles.summary: How support for public schools can help more children learn.
body: PEN’s approach focuses on improving existing government schools through stronger teaching, school facilities and digital resources.
The article explains the need for community support in schools that face shortages of resources, helping children access free quality education.

homepage.hero_tagline: FREE, QUALITY EDUCATION. FOR EVERY CHILD.
homepage.hero_caption: A smile. A school. A new beginning.
about_text: Every child has the right to a quality education. We’re here to help make that right a reality.

Founded in 2005, PEN strengthens government schools and brings digital learning to children from underserved communities. Together with teachers and supporters, we create places where children can thrive.
homepage.focus_heading: Five ways to open a world of possibility.
homepage.focus_intro: Education connects every part of our work. These five priorities bring our commitment to children, teachers and communities together.
homepage.schools_text: We work within communities to transform public schools into places of opportunity. Explore the people and places at the heart of our work.

story_text: Progressive Education Network is a professionally managed nonprofit working to bring free, quality education to children from underserved communities in Pakistan.

Since 2005, PEN has adopted public schools and supported better teaching, school facilities and digital learning. Teachers, families and supporters help turn that purpose into everyday opportunities to learn.
ceo_message: In his published message, Dr. Muhammad Najeeb Khan describes PEN’s purpose as the holistic development of children in public schools.
His priorities include better learning environments, improved school infrastructure and close collaboration with teachers, communities and partners.
The message emphasises responsible use of funds, transparency and accountability across management and school teams, with children’s academic progress at the centre of the work.
